narrative: Material PL2__M7DB30C9 exhibits smooth, high-volume demand (mean 3,501 units/day, CV 0.40) with near-perfect daily non-zero activity, making it well-suited to a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. Lead times are very short on average (0.69 days) but highly unstable (CV 1.09), making lead-time variance the dominant safety-stock driver at 85.5% of total variance. The EOQ of 20,468 units dramatically reduces ordering frequency from ~2,200 to ~43 orders/year, yielding a 95% cost reduction versus the SAP baseline while achieving the 95% service level target. The current SAP safety lead time of 3.0 days is over-conservative and should be reduced to 1.43 days.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth, near-continuous high-volume demand with stable mean justifies EOQ-driven fixed order quantities. Continuous review is appropriate given daily demand visibility and low lead times. The (r,Q) policy minimises total inventory cost while maintaining the 95% service level via a statistically derived reorder point.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Lead-time instability (CV > 1.0) is the dominant risk. Any reduction in lead-time variance would allow a material reduction in safety stock and holding costs. Storage capacity (32,583 units) is not binding: SS + OQ = 25,457 units leaves ~7,126 units headroom.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Lead-time CV exceeds 1.0 — supplier SLA review required. No MOQ-capacity infeasibility detected; policy is implementable as-is.
